nanaimo-mayor--brunie-brunie.summary: Brunie Brunie has worked in real estate sales in Vancouver, Victoria and Parksville, and earlier as a ballroom dance teacher and fashion designer. He has previously run for municipal, provincial and federal office.

nanaimo-mayor--anne-marie-dryden.summary: Anne Marie Dryden is a former independent financial advisor and Certified Financial Planner who practised for more than 35 years. She has lived in Nanaimo since 1984 and volunteers in the community.

nanaimo-mayor--leonard-krog.summary: Leonard Krog has been Mayor of Nanaimo since 2018. Born in Nanaimo and raised in Coombs, he previously served as MLA for Nanaimo and has chaired the United Way for Nanaimo.

nanaimo-mayor--sarah-lovegrove.summary: Sarah Lovegrove is a former emergency room nurse at Nanaimo Regional General Hospital who has worked with local non-profits responding to the toxic drug crisis. Originally from Ontario, she moved to Nanaimo in 2017.

nanaimo-council--jeff-annesley.summary: Jeff Annesley is a Nanaimo-born warehouse manager and published author who runs a small online publishing business. He has coached youth soccer for more than five years.

nanaimo-council--sheryl-armstrong.summary: Sheryl Armstrong is a current Nanaimo city councillor with about nine and a half years on council. She previously served 36 years as an RCMP officer.

nanaimo-council--sandy-bartlett.summary: Sandy Bartlett is a legal professional with more than 35 years of experience in commercial, real estate and family law. A Nanaimo resident for 54 years, Bartlett has been a local employer since 1990.

nanaimo-council--ken-bennett.summary: Ken Bennett has lived in Nanaimo for more than 29 years.

nanaimo-council--marnie-boers.summary: Marnie Boers is a registered nurse in the Nanaimo Regional General Hospital emergency department and a master's student in counselling. Born and raised in Nanaimo, she has worked with local shelter and support organizations.

nanaimo-council--jackie-bolen.summary: Jackie Bolen is a former teacher now working as an author, digital creator and consultant. Bolen moved to Nanaimo from the Lower Mainland and has led environmental, community garden and sports groups.

nanaimo-council--mark-chandler.summary: Mark Chandler has spent more than 40 years in food service, hospitality and distribution, founding several food businesses. He served on Parksville council from 2018 to 2022 and has lived locally since 2006.

nanaimo-council--paul-chapman.summary: Paul Chapman is a former environmental planner in Nanaimo who received the Rob Lawrance Award in 2023. He has appeared as a delegation before Nanaimo City Council on several occasions since 2018.

nanaimo-council--malcolm-cooke.summary: Malcolm Cooke studied journalism at the University of Regina and has worked in journalism and recreation. He received a Democracy Fund student journalism fellowship in 2022 and has lived in Nanaimo for four years.

nanaimo-council--andrea-coutu.summary: Andréa Coutu comes from a long-time Nanaimo family and has worked in economic analysis, project and budget management, and strategic planning, including work and volunteering in social justice and business resilience.

nanaimo-council--ryan-djakovic.summary: Ryan Djakovic is a technologist, licensed realtor and developer whose experience includes real estate, civil planning, and addictions and mental health advocacy. He has family roots in Nanaimo.

nanaimo-council--hilary-eastmure.summary: Hilary Eastmure has been a Nanaimo city councillor since 2022. A former radio reporter and federal constituency caseworker, she moved to Nanaimo in 2013 and has chaired the City's accessibility and inclusiveness committee.

nanaimo-council--joe-figel.summary: Joe Figel has more than a decade of corporate management experience and runs two family businesses in real estate and marketing. He is a director of the Brechin Hill Community Association.

nanaimo-council--meg-fyfe-watkins.summary: Meg Fyfe Watkins founded and runs a small business in downtown Nanaimo and holds a science degree. She grew up on Vancouver Island and has lived in Nanaimo for 12 years.

nanaimo-council--ben-geselbracht.summary: Ben Geselbracht is a two-term Nanaimo city councillor and registered clinical counsellor raised in Nanaimo. He co-founded a worker-owned tree service co-op and has been president of the Association of Vancouver Island and Coastal Communities.

nanaimo-council--bryan-gordon.summary: Bryan Gordon is a retired RCMP staff sergeant with more than 36 years in law enforcement, including service as a detachment commander. He has lived in Nanaimo since 2001.

nanaimo-council--patrick-gunville.summary: Patrick Gunville is a commercial real estate advisor with CBRE on the mid-Island. Raised on Vancouver Island, he is past president of the Nanaimo Executives Association and sits on the RDN Board of Variance.

nanaimo-council--derek-hanna.summary: Derek Hanna is a mechanical engineering graduate who spent 16 years at the Harmac Pacific pulp mill working on equipment and infrastructure projects. He has lived in Nanaimo since 1987.

nanaimo-council--richard-harlow.summary: Richard Harlow is a Nanaimo-born painter and small business owner. He served six years on the City's accessibility and inclusion committee and has been a CNIB ambassador and board member since 2017.

nanaimo-council--erin-hemmens.summary: Erin Hemmens is a current Nanaimo city councillor who has served on council for eight years.

nanaimo-council--steven-johns.summary: Steven Johns owns a downtown Nanaimo retail store and previously ran a local financial planning practice. A Nanaimo resident for 13 years, he is vice-chair of the Downtown Nanaimo Business Association.

nanaimo-council--cameron-leckenby.summary: Cameron Leckenby is a lifelong Nanaimo resident and VIU and UVic graduate. He has worked at BC Ferries and the Regional District of Nanaimo, and in constituency offices for two MPs and a provincial MLA.

nanaimo-council--max-mackay.summary: Max MacKay was born and raised in Nanaimo and has worked in the city's hospitality industry for seven years.

nanaimo-council--paul-manly.summary: Paul Manly is a current Nanaimo city councillor and former Member of Parliament for Nanaimo-Ladysmith. A filmmaker and former non-profit executive director, he returned to Nanaimo about 25 years ago.

nanaimo-council--bill-mckay.summary: Bill McKay was a Nanaimo city councillor from 2011 to 2014 and mayor from 2014 to 2018. A Nanaimo resident for over 20 years, he is vice-president of the Nanaimo Disability Resource Centre board.

nanaimo-council--andrew-merilees.summary: Andrew Merilees grew up in Nanaimo's Departure Bay and manages a family-owned retail store. He served four terms on Masset village council, including as mayor from 2011 to 2018.

nanaimo-council--matthew-miller.summary: Matthew Miller is a health-care worker at Nanaimo Regional General Hospital and a director of the Health Sciences Association of BC, representing health-care and social service workers on Vancouver Island.

nanaimo-council--zaki-mohammed.summary: Zaki Mohammed is a financial controller and a managing partner in two creative businesses. A Nanaimo resident for more than 10 years, he is a board director of the Central Vancouver Island Multicultural Society.

nanaimo-council--janice-perrino.summary: Janice Perrino has been a Nanaimo city councillor since 2022 and has more than 30 years in health-care leadership. She previously served two terms as a councillor and two as mayor of Summerland.

nanaimo-council--frank-pluta.summary: Frank Pluta has lived and worked in Nanaimo for more than 20 years in business roles. He previously served as a municipal councillor, regional district director and hospital board member in northern British Columbia.

nanaimo-council--austin-seng.summary: Austin Seng owns a vintage general store and photography studio in downtown Nanaimo and has more than a decade of business management experience. He has lived in Nanaimo's Harewood area for 35 years.

nanaimo-council--ian-thorpe.summary: Ian Thorpe is a current Nanaimo city councillor seeking another term.

nanaimo-council--paul-van-ryssel.summary: Paul Van Ryssel is a teacher, coach, mentor and advisor who has lived in Nanaimo for much of his adult life.

nanaimo-council--angela-hope-waldick.summary: Angela Hope Waldick is a photographer, podcaster, author and founder of Clever Creative Studios. She has studied sustainable city planning and has volunteered with a school food program and local organizations in Nanaimo.

sd68-trustee-at-large--tania-brzovic.summary: Tania Brzovic is a current SD68 trustee and lifelong Nanaimo resident who has worked in social service advocacy on anti-poverty and disability issues. She has chaired several board committees.

sd68-trustee-at-large--adrianne-cafariel.summary: Adrianne Cafariello is a social worker in health care and a parent of two children in the school system.

sd68-trustee-at-large--kailey-gillam.summary: Kailey Gillam is a parent of six and has professional leadership experience in social services.

sd68-trustee-at-large--tim-harris.summary: Tim Harris is a current SD68 trustee and former classroom teacher who spent eight and a half years as a First Nations school principal. He is a team lead with Kwumut Lelum.

sd68-trustee-at-large--leanne-lee.summary: Leanne Lee is a current SD68 trustee and chair of the Board of Education.

sd68-trustee-at-large--zeni-maartman.summary: Zeni Maartman served as an SD68 trustee from 1996 to 1999 and is a former Nanaimo city councillor and former Regional District of Nanaimo director.

sd68-trustee-at-large--fred-macdonald.summary: Fred MacDonald is a social worker with experience in addictions, rehabilitation and inclusive education, and has spent 35 years in post-secondary education, including as Dean of Trades at Vancouver Island University.

sd68-trustee-at-large--chantelle-morvay.summary: Chantelle Morvay is a current SD68 trustee who works in assessment services at Vancouver Island University. She is a former Learning Alternatives parent advisory council president.

sd68-trustee-at-large--leana-pellegrin.summary: Leana Pellegrin is a current SD68 trustee who has lived in Nanaimo for 17 years. She spent 10 years on a Nanaimo youth soccer association board and has served on the district parent advisory council.

sd68-trustee-at-large--mark-robinson.summary: Mark Robinson is a current SD68 trustee, a former ESL teacher of more than 10 years, and a community support worker with the Nanaimo Association for Community Living.

sd68-trustee-at-large--tom-rokeby.summary: Tom Rokeby is a current SD68 trustee and board vice-chair. A Nanaimo District Secondary graduate, he taught 20 years at John Barsby and holds a Master of Public Administration from the University of Victoria.

real-nanaimo.blurb: Describes itself as a coordinated team of municipal candidates (Responsible, Ethical, Accountable Leadership) sharing a governance framework built on financial discipline, community safety, transparent decision-making and local economic stability.
